universalAnswers.whatHappened: Google’s September 10 announcement says the Gemini app is available globally on Windows 10 and 11, with Alt + Space as its desktop shortcut.
universalAnswers.plainLanguageIdentity: Gemini is Google’s AI assistant; this Windows app is a desktop route into it rather than a different AI system.
universalAnswers.evidenceBasis: Google’s product announcement, Windows Help page, Workspace update and Gemini release notes were captured and reread on September 13.
universalAnswers.evidenceLimits: These are Google product sources. They establish stated requirements and functions, not local installation, every account’s availability or answer accuracy.
universalAnswers.readerRelevance: A reader deciding between a browser tab and a desktop shortcut needs to know whether the new route changes a capability, eligibility or what she shares.
universalAnswers.affectedPeople: Windows 10 and 11 users with eligible personal, work or school Google accounts; managed-account users can be limited by their administrator.
universalAnswers.changesNow: Google has added a Windows route that opens Gemini with Alt + Space beside an active task.
universalAnswers.uncertainty: Account policy, organisation settings and any connected-app access remain conditional; native Windows use was not tested in this lane.
universalAnswers.readerAction: Choose the route that is convenient, verify the account and administrator condition, and decide what you want to upload or connect.
universalAnswers.betterQuestion: Does this new interface change what the tool can do, or only make an existing function easier to reach?

company-business.businessChange: Google announced the Gemini Windows app and Alt + Space shortcut as a new desktop route for people already using Gemini.
company-business.companyMotive: Google frames the app as direct desktop assistance but the reviewed sources do not establish a measured business outcome or reader benefit.
company-business.payer: The reviewed sources do not state a personal price for the Windows app, so this candidate makes no price or subscription claim.
company-business.beneficiary: Eligible Windows users may prefer a shortcut that opens Gemini beside their active task; usefulness remains a personal convenience judgment.
company-business.incentives: No inference about Google’s commercial incentives is needed to explain this desktop release.
company-business.customerEffectNow: Where an account is eligible, the app provides a Windows route for asking questions, drafting and brainstorming; the documented administrator condition remains.
company-business.financialContext: No financial figure or reader cost is asserted because it is not needed to explain the product change.

translation.newsVersionExact: Google announced the Windows app on September 10; it is available globally for Windows 10 and 11.
translation.actualMeaningExact: The new door may save a few steps; it does not make Gemini a different kind of tool.
translation.mechanismExact: You can choose to upload an image or connect Google apps such as Gmail and Drive.
translation.familiarExampleExact: If you are revising a school-volunteer email, you could paste the draft and ask for a warmer version that keeps the date and request unchanged.

jargon.plainMeaning: connect Google apps such as Gmail and Drive

learningConnections.concept: checking what information a tool can use before sharing it
learningConnections.learningPayoff: Working with AI 101 helps readers check an AI draft before they use it in their own name.
